          About this helper

          In versions 5.0–5.2, suggestions after clues are matching words. The earliest archived solvers can also recommend information-gathering words. Probability Ranking favors familiar everyday words and common nouns, with small tone preferences. The version menu selects the ranking before a puzzle. Earlier solvers are preserved from their archived source. v5.0 gradually reduces its repeated-letter penalty as the pool shrinks, reaching zero at two candidates. In v5.2: repeated-letter words are held back while single-letter alternatives remain, excluded from the recommendation—but not the possible-word list—with 12 or more choices, strongly penalized with 7–11, moderately penalized with 4–6, and lightly penalized with 2–3. The penalty disappears when your clues indicate a repeated letter or only one word remains. Small pools favor the most plausible answer. These are estimates, not NYT probabilities. Cultural familiarity only breaks ties; there is no live news feed. Versions 5.0–5.2 always choose a possible answer on the final guess.

          Version 5.5 keeps past answers eligible and combines everyday frequency, normalized feedback entropy, a noun bonus, and your current-events list. Pattern multipliers come from the past-answer study. Above the chosen pool size it searches every dictionary word for the best split, even on the final turn; otherwise it recommends the best total-scoring possible answer. The top ten possible answers always use total score. Earlier solvers keep their original rules.

          The Panic button shows today’s New York Times Wordle answer. Answers come from published daily answer lists and are added to the page each morning.

          The definition of the word you enter appears automatically below the suggestion, shortened to two meanings. Definitions are built into the page from Wiktionary. The dark theme and dictionary work with either ranking. Completed games are recorded under the selected ranking version; existing results are preserved.

          The full word list includes uncommon accepted guesses; not every word is a likely daily answer. If you select historical answers only and those run out, the app automatically searches the full list. No three-guess guarantee.

          Word lists: Josh Stephenson, Tab Atkins, and Josh Kaufman. Independent helper; not affiliated with The New York Times. Your guesses stay in this page and clear when you reload. Completed-game statistics are saved in this browser and separated by version. WordHelper v7.5 b1 — Fri Oct 16, 2026 (Panic heading now reads HELP! I NEED THE ANSWER!; past-answers box labelled NYT). Earlier versions have no retroactive statistics.
